messages:
Alex: Heads-up — seeing a regression on nightly matmul profile after the KV-cache change. nsys + perfetto traces attached. Shapes: batched (8, 1, 8192) x (8192, 4096) with continuous batching. Tail latencies for long sequences are +25% and CPU-side scheduling looks noisy :thinking:

Maria: Ugh. Two quick suspects: 1) algo probing thrash in cuBLASLt when workspace size keeps changing, 2) workspace fragmentation because of repeated small allocations from the runtime. Can you paste the nsys top-level summary? :eyes:

Alex: Dump from nsys summary (trimmed):
```
nsys summary: Total time 60s
- cublasLtMatmul kernel group: 72.5%
- cudaMemcpy: 13.4%
- kernel launch overhead: 6.1%
- host-side scheduling: 4.0%
- memory alloc/free churn: 3.0%
Observations: repeated cublasLt algo probes (~16-22 per batch), workspace req oscillates between 2.1MB <-> 64MB depending on probed algo.
```

Alex: Perfetto flame shows periodic short spikes where GPU kernels are very small (<500us) but launched in tight succession, then a long gap while workspace allocs happen. I can share trace links privately.

Jon: That workspace oscillation screams algorithm search fallback. cuBLASLt will probe multiple algos and ask for workspaces; if the runtime returns "no workspace" it will try a smaller one, causing multiple launches. Two things to try: pin a preferred algo for this shape or set a stable workspace pool so allocs don't block.

Maria: Can you reproduce with a nvprof-like capture? Also run a targeted cublasLt probe that lists candidate algos and their required workspace sizes:
```
// pseudo
cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetList(handle, desc, algos, &count);
for (i=0;i<count;i++) cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetWorkspace(handle, desc, algos[i], &workspace_bytes);
```
That'll show which algos flip between tiny and big workspace.

PerfBot: Auto-report from last nsys run: 
- avg cublasLtMatmul (device kernel) per call: 3.2ms
- algo_probe_count per logical matmul: 19 (stddev 4)
- avg workspace_alloc size during probe phase: 28.3MB
- memcpy stall windows: 420ms total across trace
(see /internal/traces/2003456789/nsys_summary.html) :robot_face:

Sam: Quick workaround patch that helped in a local repro: prefer cuBLAS non-probing path for these shapes by setting a heuristic override. In our runtime config: 
```
// in runtime heuristics
if (shape.batch==8 && A.k==8192 && B.n==4096) {
  algorithm_preference = "cublas_fixed_algo=6"; // lock to algo 6 which is stable for this shape
  prefer_workspace_pool = true;
}
```
That cut probe_count to ~1 and reduced tail by ~18% in my run. Not a long-term fix but useful for customer rollouts.

Maria: Nice. We should also instrument KV-cache warmup to avoid triggering probes during latency-sensitive windows. If KV warmup triggers many small queries that cause transient shape patterns, the scheduler will interleave probes and cause global noise.

Jon: Agreed. Another low-risk change: keep a tiny persistent scratch buffer per device for cuBLASLt scratch allocations (64MB reserved) and return that as available workspace during probe. Prevents blocking allocs and reduces fragmentation. Pseudocode: 
```
device_scratch = cudaMalloc(64MB);
on_probe_request(size) {
  if (size <= 64MB) return device_scratch;
  else return cudaMalloc(size);
}
```
Tradeoff: slightly higher reserved GPU memory but much lower probe jitter.

Alex: Good set of action items — I'll: 1) run the cublasLt algo list probe and paste results, 2) spin a test with Sam's heuristic override, 3) try the persistent scratch pool. Will post new traces. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Maria: If you post the perfetto flame snippet, I can annotate hotspots and propose a micro-scheduling fix for the runtime.

PerfBot: Added labels to trace: possible_workspace_frag, frequent_algo_probe, kvcache-warmup-spike.

Alex: Uploaded perfetto snippet at /internal/traces/2003456789/perfetto_flame.html — highlights at 00:02:14 and 00:03:07 where probe bursts align with KV cache refills.

Sam: I'll open a small PR with the heuristic override and scratch-pool change, mark it WIP and link to this thread.

Jon: When you open the PR, include a small micro-benchmark: B=4096, K=8192, batch=8, and compare three configs: probe-enabled, algo-locked, scratch-pool. That'll make rollout decision easier.

Alex: Will do. Thanks! :rocket:
